pages.text: The rain came down all night. In the morning, Yaa opened the door and gasped. The lane outside her house was a brown river, and her school shoes were floating in it.
sentences: The rain came down all night.
In the morning, Yaa opened the door and gasped.
The lane outside her house was a brown river, and her school shoes were floating in it.
pages.alt: A girl in a doorway looks out at a flooded lane with her school shoes floating on the water.

pages.text: ‘Why is the water still here?’ Yaa asked. Her brother Kofi shrugged. ‘It is only rain,’ he said. But Yaa remembered what her teacher said: when something puzzles you, do not guess. Look closely, and find out.
sentences: ‘Why is the water still here?’ Yaa asked.
Her brother Kofi shrugged.
‘It is only rain,’ he said.
But Yaa remembered what her teacher said: when something puzzles you, do not guess.
Look closely, and find out.
pages.alt: Yaa crouches at the edge of the water, looking closely, while her younger brother shrugs.

pages.text: Yaa followed the water along the lane to the open drain beside the road. It was supposed to carry the rain away to the stream. But today, the water was piling up in front of it like a crowd at a gate.
sentences: Yaa followed the water along the lane to the open drain beside the road.
It was supposed to carry the rain away to the stream.
But today, the water was piling up in front of it like a crowd at a gate.
pages.alt: Yaa walks beside the flooded lane to an open roadside drain where water is piling up.

pages.text: Yaa knelt and looked in. The drain was packed with plastic bottles, torn sachets, old bags and mud. ‘The rain cannot get through,’ she said slowly. ‘It has nowhere to go.’
sentences: Yaa knelt and looked in.
The drain was packed with plastic bottles, torn sachets, old bags and mud.
‘The rain cannot get through,’ she said slowly.
‘It has nowhere to go.’
pages.alt: Yaa kneels at the drain and sees it packed with plastic bottles, bags and mud.

pages.text: That afternoon, Yaa made a plan. She drew a map of the lane in her exercise book and marked every place where rubbish was dropped. Then she counted. In one afternoon, she counted forty-two bottles and sachets near the drain.
sentences: That afternoon, Yaa made a plan.
She drew a map of the lane in her exercise book and marked every place where rubbish was dropped.
Then she counted.
In one afternoon, she counted forty-two bottles and sachets near the drain.
pages.alt: Yaa draws a map of the lane in her exercise book and counts rubbish, with numbers beside her marks.

pages.text: At the weekend, Yaa knocked on doors. ‘Please, can we clear the drain together?’ she asked. Some neighbours said they were too busy. But Auntie Akosua brought a broom, Mr Mensah brought a wheelbarrow, and soon a whole line of people stood by the drain.
sentences: At the weekend, Yaa knocked on doors.
‘Please, can we clear the drain together?’ she asked.
Some neighbours said they were too busy.
But Auntie Akosua brought a broom, Mr Mensah brought a wheelbarrow, and soon a whole line of people stood by the drain.
pages.alt: Neighbours with brooms, a wheelbarrow and gloves gather beside the drain with Yaa.

pages.text: They worked all morning. They scooped out the mud and sorted the rubbish into piles: plastic to be collected for recycling, and the rest to be taken to the proper bin. Slowly, with a gurgle and a rush, the water began to move.
sentences: They worked all morning.
They scooped out the mud and sorted the rubbish into piles: plastic to be collected for recycling, and the rest to be taken to the proper bin.
Slowly, with a gurgle and a rush, the water began to move.
pages.alt: Neighbours scoop mud and sort plastic into piles beside the drain as the water begins to flow.

pages.text: ‘It works!’ cried Kofi. The water ran down the drain and away to the stream, and the lane slowly turned from river to road again. Yaa smiled. But she knew the job was not finished.
sentences: ‘It works!’ cried Kofi.
The water ran down the drain and away to the stream, and the lane slowly turned from river to road again.
Yaa smiled.
But she knew the job was not finished.
pages.alt: The lane drying out as water flows away down the cleared drain; Kofi cheering.

pages.text: On Monday, Yaa spoke at her school assembly. ‘A drain only works if we keep it clear,’ she said. ‘Every bottle in the drain is a little wall. If we put it in the bin, we keep the water moving.’ Her classmates nodded, and the head teacher asked her to lead a Clean Lane Club.
sentences: On Monday, Yaa spoke at her school assembly.
‘A drain only works if we keep it clear,’ she said.
‘Every bottle in the drain is a little wall.
If we put it in the bin, we keep the water moving.’ Her classmates nodded, and the head teacher asked her to lead a Clean Lane Club.
pages.alt: Yaa speaks at a school assembly while classmates listen and the head teacher smiles.

pages.text: By the next rainy season, the lane stayed dry. Each week, the club checked the drain, counted the rubbish and wrote the number on a chart. After one month, the number had gone from forty-two to six. Yaa looked at the chart and smiled. Counting had shown her the problem, and counting showed her it was getting better.
sentences: By the next rainy season, the lane stayed dry.

pages.alt: Yaa and club members beside the clean drain, pointing at a chart of falling numbers.
